prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key proposals and commitments (2010)

Economy and public finances
- Support the recovery now; more than halve the deficit by 2014 via growth, targeted spending cuts, and tax measures (including a 1p rise in National Insurance, reduced pension tax relief for highest earners, a 50p top rate, and a bank bonus tax).
- Protect frontline spending on childcare, schools, the NHS and policing; deliver £20bn annual efficiencies by 2012-13; cap most public-sector pay rises at 1% for 2011-13; reform public sector pensions; raise £20bn from asset sales by 2020.
- Reform banking: higher capital, “living wills,” a global levy, tougher pay oversight, increased competition, and disposal/possible mutualisation options for state-controlled assets.
- Industrial strategy: UK Finance for Growth (£4bn), Green Investment Bank, R&D tax credits, patent box, enhanced capital allowances, and export support.
- Infrastructure: High Speed Rail (phased link North–South), Crossrail completion, rail electrification, expanded motorway hard-shoulder running, 100,000 EV charging points, and universal/superfast broadband funded partly by a landline levy.

Jobs, welfare, housing and personal finance
- Job guarantees: placements for young people at six months; mandatory job offer after two years’ unemployment; expanded apprenticeships and Skills Accounts.
- Minimum wage to rise at least with average earnings; “Better Off in Work” £40/week guarantee.
- Reassess 1.5m incapacity claims; tighten Housing Benefit rules; crack down on fraud.
- First-time buyer stamp duty holiday up to £250k for two years (funded by 5% rate above £1m); build 110,000 affordable homes; enable councils to build up to 10,000 homes/year by end of Parliament; National Landlord Register; aim to end rough sleeping by 2012.
- Savings: higher ISA limits (index-linked); Savings Gateway; matched savings for 18–30 basic-rate taxpayers; protect Child Trust Fund and boost for disabled children.
- Consumer finance: People’s Bank via Post Office; universal basic bank account right; levy to expand affordable credit; regulate high-cost lending; single consumer credit regulator.

Education
- Increase frontline funding for Sure Start/childcare, schools and 16–19; expand free nursery for 2–4s; one-to-one/small group “3Rs” catch-up; parents can trigger leadership changes in underperforming schools; up to 1,000 schools in accredited groups by 2015.
- Personal tutors in secondary; broader academic/vocational routes; behaviour enforcement; extended school day care; raise participation to 18; expand advanced apprenticeships; widen access to higher education.

Health and care
- Legal guarantees: 18-week treatment or funded private option; cancer results within one week of referral; health checks for ages 40–74; right to choose qualified NHS-cost providers and evening/weekend GP access.
- More home and community care, one-to-one cancer nursing, expanded psychological therapies; £20bn NHS efficiencies; expand Foundation Trusts and performance management.
- National Care Service: from 2011 free home care for highest needs; from 2014 cap residential care costs after two years; long-term financing commission; restore earnings link for State Pension from 2012; end default retirement at 65; “Fathers’ Month” and more flexible leave.

Policing, justice and immigration
- Maintain police/PCSO numbers; 80% neighbourhood time on the beat; online report cards; replace failing leadership/units.
- Faster action on anti-social behaviour, including right to injunctions; expand Community Payback.
- Use DNA/CCTV within safeguards; expand prisons to 96,000 by 2014; virtual courts; enhanced victims’ services.
- Points-based immigration system with stronger border controls; no unskilled migration from outside the EU; tougher English requirements; limit access to benefits/housing to citizens and permanent residents.

Culture, communities and environment
- Deliver 2012 Olympics legacy; expand school sport; strengthen supporter ownership options in football; maintain free museum entry; protect post offices and viable pubs; Social Investment Bank and community ownership support.
- Low-carbon plan: ~40% low-carbon electricity by 2020; 400,000 green jobs by 2015; renewables, new nuclear, CCS for coal; smart meters by 2020; “Pay As You Save” home upgrades; stronger insulation standards; toward zero waste; expand habitats/woodland; maintain Green Belt; Supermarkets Ombudsman.

Constitution and governance
- Referendums on Alternative Vote for Commons and an elected second chamber (staged); fixed-term Parliaments; lobbyist register; restrictions on MPs’ outside roles; potential voting age reduction to 16 after citizenship education improvements; expand open data and local accountability; greater city-region powers; review local government finance.

Foreign policy and defence
- Afghanistan strategy focused on security transition; additional equipment and training.
- Strategic Defence Review; maintain independent nuclear deterrent; modernise forces; enhance veterans’ support and entitlements.
- Active EU role (including enlargement and climate leadership); reform UN/IFIs/G20/NATO; commit 0.7% of national income to aid from 2013 in law; drive progress on health, education, water/sanitation, anti-corruption and fair trade.
